title: Attitudes and Values
description: Put money on trial and give your opinion about it with the words of lesson 12 (root, evil, corruption, tyranny, dignity, decent, appeal, cheating, revenge, anarchy, calamity, to make ends meet, right away); name a result the way careful written English does, with therefore and as a result, two conjunctive adverbs, and that's why, which is a clause and not an adverb at all - what makes the first two adverbs and not conjunctions, the semicolon or the full stop they need in front of them, the comma they take after them, the three places they may stand inside a clause and the register each one belongs to; instruct and direct others with the imperative - base verb with no subject, don't + base verb for a prohibition, let's + base verb when the order includes the speaker, please and the tag will you? when it has to be softened, and its five values (instruction, advice, warning, prohibition, invitation); speak of freedom and of what a community owes itself (rights, duties, peace, community, to forgive, precious, freedom) and hear the three sounds of the lesson, the vowel of love, the vowel of sound and the consonant of expression; and finally ask for agreement with the question tag - the auxiliary that comes back, the polarity that turns over, the pronoun that replaces the subject, the special cases aren't I, shall we, will you, isn't there and everybody ... they, the falling voice that asks for confirmation against the rising voice that really asks, and the yes or no that answers the fact and never the shape of the question - all through the adjectives that judge a character (honest, truthful, tolerant, trustworthy, reliable, faithful, loving, correct, insincere, jealous, suspicious, deceitful, shameful, indifferent, immoral, corrupt) and the language of a debate (giving your opinion, disagreeing politely, offering your reasons)
